clue.text: Woman as wife receiving good time

indicators.note: the word for wife takes in the letter for good, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a bride is a newly married wife

explanation.surface: A woman marries and, as a wife, enjoys a pleasant time.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridget is a female given name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: What sheep produce, including meat, in islands

indicators.note: the bleats hold the meat inside them

parts.note: sheep produce baas, their bleats
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: Sheep giving wool and mutton on some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What sheep produce' suggests wool, but it is their bleats.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bahamas is an island nation in the Atlantic, a group of islands.

clue.text: European support for drift netting fish is urgent

indicators.note: in a down entry the European letter sits below, supporting the rest
the meaning word catches the fish inside it

parts.note: drift means import, the gist or meaning
tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A European is urged to support drift-netting of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drift' looks like fishing with drift nets but means gist.
explanation.definitionFit: Importunate means persistent and pressing in demands, close to urgent.

clue.text: Flag day can be organised, not a persistent irritant

indicators.note: the letters of the two words can be arranged differently
the letter of 'a' is excluded from the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A charity flag day can be arranged without becoming a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'Flag day' are the answer plus the A that 'not a' leaves out. A flag day is a British street collection for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadfly is a horsefly, and figuratively a person who keeps annoying others.

clue.text: Is it honest to tell stories about female? Very like

parts.note: true means honest, as in a true friend

indicators.note: the word for telling stories goes round the letter for female

parts.note: to tell stories can mean to lie

explanation.surface: A question about whether it is honest to fib about a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something realistic closely resembles the real thing, which is what very like means.

clue.text: Very hot place includes one cold area, like a spring

indicators.note: the hot place holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: hell is proverbially the hottest place there is
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A description of a sweltering spot with one cool patch, oddly compared to springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but here it is a coiled metal spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiled spring has a spiral shape, which is the meaning of helical.

clue.text: In good health, say hello

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, so it sounds like another

parts.note: hail is a greeting, a way to say hello

explanation.surface: Someone in good health is told to greet people.
explanation.definitionFit: Hale means strong and healthy, as in 'hale and hearty'.

clue.text: Offering freedom to depose king

indicators.note: the king is removed from the word for freedom

parts.note: liberation is freedom
ER is a royal cipher, Edward Rex for king

explanation.surface: A people offers freedom on the condition of removing the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is a drink poured out as an offering to a god.

clue.text: Caught greeting some foreign character

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A greeting overheard from a foreign person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter of an alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a foreign character.

clue.text: These days in character, virtually, as binge-drinker

indicators.note: the time phrase goes inside the shortened character
virtually means almost, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a letter is a written character
AD, anno Domini, marks the current era

explanation.surface: Describes someone nowadays playing the part of a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' removes the last letter of LETTER, leaving LETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a young woman given to loud, boozy behaviour, a British stereotype of the 1990s.

clue.text: Start to cheer seeing flask here?

definitions.meaning: the opening word of the cheer '..., ..., hooray'
a ... flask is carried at the ...

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates at the sight of a flask of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Three cheers begin with the call 'hip, hip', and a pocket flask is named for the body part where it sits.

clue.text: Such an experiment puts learner into dilemma

indicators.note: the learner's letter is put inside the phrase for dilemma

parts.note: a double bind is a dilemma with no good way out
L is the learner symbol, from L-plates on British cars

explanation.surface: An experiment that traps the student in an awkward dilemma.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial where neither subjects nor researchers know who gets what is the classic kind of controlled experiment named this way.

clue.text: Ancient drama exam during college year

indicators.note: the exam happens inside the college, so it goes within its letters

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Someone sits an exam on ancient drama during their college year.
explanation.definitionFit: A morality play is a medieval allegorical drama, so the word names an old form of theatre.

clue.text: Stretch of water has singular characteristic

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: A particular channel of sea is said to have a unique feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow channel joining two seas, such as the one at Dover, is a stretch of water.

clue.text: Badly miscast, go in disbelief

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: An actor is wrongly cast and goes into the role incredulous.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnosticism is doubt about God's existence, a form of religious disbelief.

clue.text: No shortened undergarment is accepted by little scientist

indicators.note: the inner pieces are taken in by the word for little

parts.note: a bit means a little
no can mean zero, written O

indicators.note: the last letter of the garment is cut off

parts.note: a chemise is a woman's loose undergarment

explanation.surface: A small scientist refuses a skimpy undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A biochemist is a scientist who studies chemical processes in living things.

clue.text: Very high course

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
up means high, as in 'up in the air'

explanation.surface: Describes a lofty course, perhaps a steep golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a dinner course, not a route or golf links.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is often served as the first course of a meal.

clue.text: Having illness, one ignorant man drinks nothing — not even this?

parts.note: flu is a common illness
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the dunce takes in the zero, so it goes inside him

parts.note: a dunce is a slow-witted person
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sick, foolish man who drinks nothing at all, not even a drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not even this?' plays on the phrase 'not a drop': the sick teetotaller won't take even the smallest liquid measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny measure of liquid volume, the smallest amount someone abstaining might refuse.

clue.text: Very desirable of editor to edit

indicators.note: editing changes text, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editor is keen to revise something.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something so desirable one would sacrifice anything for it.

clue.text: Pocketing a pound, departing old deputy makes room for president

indicators.note: the deputy's word holds the other letters as in a pocket

parts.note: vice, as in vice-president, means a deputy
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
off means departing, as in 'we're off'

explanation.surface: A retiring deputy pockets a pound and makes room for the new president.
explanation.definitionFit: The president of the United States works in this oval-shaped room in the White House.

clue.text: Written work absorbs new copyist

indicators.note: the work takes the letter for new inside

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
an aper is one who apes, a copier

explanation.surface: A piece of written work contains a new copyist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set down in writing is said to be committed to paper, i.e. written.

clue.text: Notice me polishing small silver tray for starters

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone polishing a small silver tray calls for attention.
explanation.definitionFit: This whispered sound is used to attract someone's attention discreetly.

clue.text: Woman in labour may need this cut?

definitions.text: Woman in labour may need this cut?

parts.words: Woman in labour may need this cut?
parts.note: a heavily pregnant woman cannot reach her own feet to trim her nails, so someone must do it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a surgical cut in childbirth, but the real point is she cannot bend down to her toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail on the foot needs trimming, a task late pregnancy makes hard.

clue.text: Indian puts hand on part of leg, turning head away

parts.note: paw is informal for a hand

indicators.note: the first letter of the leg part is removed

parts.note: the knee is part of the leg

explanation.surface: An Indian puts a hand on someone's knee and looks away.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pawnee are a Native American people, so a member is an American Indian.

clue.text: In summary, parking is right beside playing field

indicators.note: the word 'is' goes on the right side of the playing field

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
a rec is a recreation ground, a British public playing field

explanation.surface: A short report on where the parking is next to the sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a brief summary of a text.

clue.text: Buy some biography to extend one's horizons

parts.note: to get something can mean to buy it
a means some, a single one
a life is a written account of someone's life, a biography

explanation.surface: Advice to purchase a biography to broaden your outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a retort telling someone to broaden their interests and do more with their days.

clue.text: Youthful problem Isaac Newton looked into? On the contrary

indicators.note: rather than Newton studying the answer, the answer sits inside his name

explanation.surface: Did Newton research teenage spots?
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin complaint typical of adolescence, so a youthful problem.

clue.text: Film material for paper and some literature

parts.note: pulp is the mashed wood fibre paper is made from
fiction is a body of imaginative literature

explanation.surface: A list of what paper and books are made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino's 1994 crime movie has this title.

clue.text: The French department is to be knocked down

definitions.meaning: one of the administrative departments of France, named after its river
an item to be sold at auction, knocked down by the hammer

explanation.surface: A French region is slated for demolition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lot is a department in south-west France, and an auction item is a lot.

clue.text: Princess may sound a duck

indicators.note: the answer is said like the duck's name in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck

explanation.surface: A princess might make a noise like a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the duck's name ends without an R, so it matches the princess's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Ida is the title heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.

clue.text: He's not working on Scottish island

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
Tiree is an island of the Inner Hebrides in Scotland

explanation.surface: A man on a Scottish island has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has stopped working for good in old age is a pensioner of this kind.

clue.text: One may give you a lift -—- it's left to Sandhurst

definitions.text: One may give you a lift

indicators.note: the letter for left is added to the end of the Sandhurst phrase

parts.note: Sandhurst is the RMA, the Royal Military Academy, written here with the article

explanation.surface: A soldier's lift has been left to the military academy at Sandhurst.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst is the British army officers' academy, the RMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising column of warm air lifts gliders and birds, so it can give a lift.
